task.title: Revision-owned optimistic form
task.specification: config={fields:object}. Start revision=0,status='idle',pending={}. edit={type:'edit',set:object,remove:[keys]} applies removals then sets, increments revision even if no-op, and status=idle. submit={type:'submit',id,set:object,remove:[keys]} for an ID never previously submitted saves the pre-submit fields, applies the same patch, increments revision, records that revision, makes this ID current owner, and sets status=saving; repeated IDs are ignored. success={type:'success',id,fields:object} or failure={type:'failure',id} removes a known pending submission. It can change form fields/status ONLY if it is current owner AND its recorded revision equals current revision. Such success replaces fields with server fields, increments revision,status=saved; such failure restores its saved pre-submit fields, increments revision,status=error. Both clear current owner. Other known outcomes only remove pending; unknown/repeated outcomes are ignored. A newer user edit or submission protects newer values from old outcomes. Output {fields,revision,status,pending:[sorted unsettled IDs]}. Null is a real value, deletion uses remove. Return one output per event. State is opaque JSON, initially null. Output objects have exactly the documented keys; object key order is irrelevant, array order is significant. IDs are nonempty ASCII strings. Values are JSON scalars unless stated otherwise. Numeric values and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers; integral JSON notations such as 1 and 1.0 denote the same number, while booleans are distinct. Strings contain Unicode scalar values without unpaired surrogates. Inputs have at most 48 events and eight simultaneous identities. Ordinary instances vary values; boundary instances emphasize empty/disabled/equality/no-op states; adversarial instances reorder callbacks and interleave edits; shift instances use longer traces/more identities within the same rules. These tasks test controller state/effects only, not visual quality, browser integration or screen-reader usability.

matchedCard.label: Lighthouse sector signals
matchedCard.relation: A navigational source can provide a general identifying signal and a separate directional indication for a particular hazard. What a sector indication signifies depends on the observer's position and its relationship to the marked region.
assumptions: The source and the meaning of its sector can be identified.
The observer has sufficient visibility and positional context to interpret the indication.
matchedCard.boundary: A sector signal describes only its designated region. An ordinary indication does not certify that every nearby route is hazard-free, and poor visibility can limit interpretation.
matchedCard.source_fact: Trinity House describes Start Point's white navigational flashes and a separate red sector marking the shallow Skerries Bank, alongside a low-visibility hazard warning signal.

sources.title: Trinity House completes re-engineering of Start Point Lighthouse

shuffledCard.label: Cartographic generalization
shuffledCard.relation: At a smaller representation scale, selection, simplification, and combination can preserve legibility while omitting detail. The resulting representation depends on scale and purpose; omission from that representation does not establish absence from the represented world.
assumptions: The representation has a specified scale and communicative purpose.
A more detailed source contains distinctions from which the representation is derived.
shuffledCard.boundary: Simplification can remove a distinction important for another purpose. A reduced representation cannot recover information that it does not encode.
shuffledCard.source_fact: USGS describes cartographic generalization as selecting and reducing detail to produce representations appropriate to scale.

initial.explanation: Rule: an outcome may mutate visible form state only when its submission is still the current owner and its recorded revision equals the current revision; otherwise it only settles its own pending ID. A newer edit or submission changes the revision, protecting newer values. Counterexample: restoring an old submission after an edit would overwrite the newer edit.
initial.mapping: Maps each submission ID to {before,revision}; maps global owner and revision to the authorization condition for success/failure; maps pending IDs to unsettled submissions.
initial.assumptions: JSON values are finite and inputs satisfy the stated event and identity constraints. Object key order is irrelevant; IDs sort lexically.

final.explanation: Each accepted submission stores its pre-submit fields and the revision created by that submission. An outcome mutates visible state only when its ID is still the current owner and its recorded revision equals the current revision; otherwise it merely settles that submission. Edits and new submissions advance the revision, protecting newer values from stale callbacks.

initial.explanation: Each submission owns the revision it creates and stores a pre-submit snapshot. Outcomes may settle their own pending record, but only the current owner at the same revision may alter fields. Edits and newer submissions therefore protect newer values.
initial.mapping: The controller maps fields, revision, status, pending records, submission history, and current owner directly to the specified form state and causal guards.
initial.assumptions: Inputs are valid JSON under the stated contract; field values are scalar JSON values and IDs are nonempty ASCII strings.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var s=null;for(var i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){var x=solve({config:input.config,state:s,event:input.events[i]});if(JSON.stringify(x.output)!==JSON.stringify(output[i]))return false;s=x.state}return true}

final.explanation: Each submission records its pre-submit fields and the revision it creates. An outcome always settles its known pending ID, but it changes form data only when that submission is still the current owner at the same revision. Edits and newer submissions increment the revision, protecting newer values from stale callbacks.

initial.explanation: Track each submission’s pre-submit snapshot and revision. A callback may commit only while its submission remains current and no newer revision exists; otherwise it merely settles the pending request.
initial.mapping: Submission IDs map to pending records, permanent seen IDs, a current owner, and the revision captured at submission. Edits and submissions advance revision; accepted outcomes advance it again.
initial.assumptions: Object fields contain JSON scalar values, so shallow object copies preserve all required data. Lexicographic JavaScript sorting matches the required sorted ID order.
initial.holds: function holds(input,out){if(!Array.isArray(out)||out.length!==input.events.length)return false;var s=null,h=[],p=[],own=null;function cp(x){var y={};for(var k in x)y[k]=x[k];return y}function patch(f,e){(e.remove||[]).forEach(function(k){delete f[k]});for(var k in(e.set||{}))f[k]=e.set[k]}function eq(a,b){return JSON.stringify(a)===JSON.stringify(b)}s={f:cp(input.config.fields),r:0,t:'idle'};for(var i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){var e=input.events[i],q=s.f;if(e.type==='edit'){patch(q,e);s.r++;s.t='idle'}else if(e.type==='submit'){if(h.indexOf(e.id)<0){h.push(e.id);p.push({id:e.id,b:cp(q),r:s.r+1});patch(q,e);s.r++;own=e.id;s.t='saving'}}else if(e.type==='success'||e.type==='failure'){var z=-1;for(var j=0;j<p.length;j++)if(p[j].id===e.id)z=j;if(z>=0){var a=p[z];p.splice(z,1);if(own===e.id&&a.r===s.r){if(e.type==='success'){s.f=cp(e.fields);s.r++;s.t='saved'}else{s.f=a.b;s.r++;s.t='error'}own=null}}}var ids=p.map(function(x){return x.id}).sort(),want={fields:s.f,revision:s.r,status:s.t,pending:ids};if(!eq(out[i],want))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(!s)s={f:cp(c.fields),r:0,t:'idle',h:[],p:[],o:null};var f=s.f;if(e.type==='edit'){patch(f,e);s.r++;s.t='idle'}else if(e.type==='submit'){if(s.h.indexOf(e.id)<0){s.h.push(e.id);s.p.push({id:e.id,b:cp(f),r:s.r+1});patch(f,e);s.r++;s.o=e.id;s.t='saving'}}else if(e.type==='success'||e.type==='failure'){var n=-1;for(var i=0;i<s.p.length;i++)if(s.p[i].id===e.id)n=i;if(n>=0){var q=s.p[n];s.p.splice(n,1);if(s.o===e.id&&q.r===s.r){if(e.type==='success'){s.f=cp(e.fields);s.r++;s.t='saved'}else{s.f=q.b;s.r++;s.t='error'}s.o=null}}}var ids=s.p.map(function(q){return q.id}).sort();return{state:s,output:{fields:s.f,revision:s.r,status:s.t,pending:ids}}}function cp(x){var y={};for(var k in x)y[k]=x[k];return y}function patch(f,e){(e.remove||[]).forEach(function(k){delete f[k]});for(var k in(e.set||{}))f[k]=e.set[k]}

final.explanation: Maintains fields, revision, status, permanently seen submission IDs, unsettled records, and current owner. Each accepted submission snapshots pre-submit fields and records its resulting revision. Outcomes always settle known pending submissions, but mutate form state only when still owned and revision-matched; stale outcomes are ignored for state changes.
final.program: function solve(x){var e=x.event,s=x.state;if(!s)s={f:cp(x.config.fields),r:0,t:'idle',h:[],p:[],o:null};var f=s.f;if(e.type==='edit'){patch(f,e);s.r++;s.t='idle'}else if(e.type==='submit'){if(s.h.indexOf(e.id)<0){s.h.push(e.id);s.p.push({id:e.id,b:cp(f),r:s.r+1});patch(f,e);s.r++;s.o=e.id;s.t='saving'}}else if(e.type==='success'||e.type==='failure'){var n=-1;for(var i=0;i<s.p.length;i++)if(s.p[i].id===e.id){n=i;break}if(n>=0){var q=s.p[n];s.p.splice(n,1);if(s.o===e.id&&q.r===s.r){if(e.type==='success'){s.f=cp(e.fields);s.r++;s.t='saved'}else{s.f=q.b;s.r++;s.t='error'}s.o=null}}}return{state:s,output:{fields:s.f,revision:s.r,status:s.t,pending:s.p.map(function(q){return q.id}).sort()}}}function cp(x){var y={};for(var k in x)y[k]=x[k];return y}function patch(f,e){var a=e.remove||[];for(var i=0;i<a.length;i++)delete f[a[i]];for(var k in(e.set||{}))f[k]=e.set[k]}
